sound and captions.heard:
All 12 questions were asked on the 08:22 render; two of its shots have since been replaced.

Voices. Timo: a young adult man, mid-to-low, General American, "clean studio" sound. The watcher called his four spoken lines one voice both times ("SAME VOICE"), which fits the measured pitch of 122-170 Hz. Luna: both times it said the voice changes. "It's the small one" was child-like, squeaky and sing-song; "Trust me" adult, low and calm; "It can't come in, Timo" young adult, medium and deadpan. Verdict: "DIFFERENT VOICES" (measured 350, 189 and 245 Hz). With the picture blacked out it heard two voices: a man doing a "straight-man cartoon voice" and a woman "high-pitched, squeaky, hyperactive... like an anime character".

Understanding. Every captioned line was written down correctly except "a small one". "Too slow!" was the only line it called hard to understand.

Mouths. Fine for Timo's first line and for Luna's lines in shot 1 and at the gate; "entirely absent" for "love this suitcase".

Music. With the picture: "modern Afro-pop / dance-pop... current social-video beat". Blind, and told to be picky: "royalty-free stock music, EDM-lite vlog background", "mixed quietly"; yet it guessed the clip to be "an ordinary creator's funny video", not an advert or a children's show. It heard no chant and no clap pattern on the ride. The first four seconds were "quite quiet... can be quiet on low-volume phone speakers", clearly audible from 4-5 s. The drop was "exactly on the cut" once and "slightly after" once; measured, it is 0.14 s after.

Mix. It found nothing distorted and missed any wheel sound on the ride. The quiet before the logo read as a deliberate pause. It called the laugh on the logo "pitch-shifted / processed, chipmunk-like" twice; that laugh has since been replaced.

How far to trust it. It contradicts itself on pitch ("Trust me" was "high, childlike" in one answer and low or mid-range in two), on how loud the opening music is and on how the music ends, and it invented picture details in the cat shot. I relied on it only where two answers agree or a measurement backs it.

Solid in both renders:
- All six captioned lines are read back word for word from the final mix by two recognisers, apart from the doubtful "the"/"a" in Luna's first line; each caption appears within 0.07 s of the voice.
- Loudness is -14.1 LUFS with a true peak of -1.9 dB; no clipping, no click at any cut, mono-safe.

2. Timo says "I love this suitcase" through a frozen grin.
3. On a phone speaker the music nearly vanishes, and blind it was called stock music. The trendy music the client asked for is not audibly there.

5. Both cat sounds are the loudest things in the film.
